site.deleteHint: The site, its files, database and staging copy will be deleted. This cannot be undone.
site.emptyHint: Launch a production-ready WordPress site in one click.
site.newHint: Every site is isolated, cached and backed up with verified restores.
site.title: Site title

profileHint.commerce: strict bypass for cart and checkout

overview.stagingHint: Clone production, test changes, then publish them with Safe Push.
overview.velocityHint: Full-page cache with request coalescing and stale-while-revalidate.

cache.purgeHint: On WordPress, content edits already purge the right pages. This is for everything else.

wp.adminHint: Open wp-admin in one click, no password needed.
wp.name: Name
wp.objectCacheHint: In-memory query cache (APCu): faster admin, cart and uncached pages.
wp.warmHint: Fills the cache from the sitemap so the first visitor never finds it cold.

staging.diffHint: Files changed on staging, to review before publishing.
staging.diffTruncated: List truncated: there are more differences than shown.
staging.noChanges: Staging and production have the same files.
staging.noneHint: A private, password-protected copy of production to try changes on.
staging.probePathsHint: Performance Guard compares these pages between staging and production.
staging.pushHint: Performance Guard measures staging and production; if staging is slower, publishing is blocked.
staging.pushStarted: Safe Push started: Performance Guard is comparing staging with production
staging.recreateCard: Replaces staging with a fresh copy of production.
staging.recreateHint: The current staging copy, files and database, will be replaced with a fresh copy of production.
staging.safePushHint: Publishes staging's code only if it does not make the site slower.
staging.tablesCard: Copies only the chosen tables to production. Orders, users and sessions are protected.
staging.tablesHint: The chosen production tables will be replaced with staging's. A safety snapshot is taken first.
staging.cloning: Cloning… the comparison appears once the copy is complete.

deploy.noneHint: Publish from staging with Safe Push, create one from a folder above, or release with cgctl.
deploy.rollbackHint: Goes straight back to the previous release.
deploy.rollbackTitle: Roll back to the previous release?

note.drift: The site serves this release; the records said another was live.
note.regressed: Regressed after its promotion; the automatic rollback failed.

deploy.intro: Every release is a folder of its own: activating one only moves the current link, so going back is instant.
deploy.newReleaseHint: Copies a folder of the site into a release. Nothing in it is run; activate it when it is ready.
deploy.checkoutHint: The folders under src/, where the site’s SSH shell clones and pulls.
deploy.noCheckouts: No checkout under src/ yet: turn on the SSH shell (SFTP tab) and clone your repository into ~/src.
deploy.folderHint: A folder under shared/, such as shared/build, uploaded over SFTP: the site's own top folder is read-only.

backup.deleteHint: It is removed from the repository together with its database backup. This cannot be undone.
backup.deleteKept: The newest backup that passed its restore test, and one whose test has not run yet, cannot be deleted.
backup.noneHint: Backups run on the site's schedule, and each is checked with a test restore.
backup.restoreHint: A fresh safety backup is taken before restoring.
backup.safety: A fresh safety snapshot is created before the site is touched.
backup.scheduleHint: A backup counts only once its restore test has passed: every snapshot is restored aside and checked.
backup.stagingHint: A staging copy has no schedule of its own: production’s backups cover the site.
backup.retentionHint: 0 keeps every snapshot. Older ones are removed once a day; the newest verified one always stays.
backup.retentionAdmin: Only an administrator changes how long backups are kept.
backup.destinationHint: Set in the server’s settings, for every site.
backup.noRepository: No backup repository is configured yet: backups cannot run.
backup.everySnapshot: every snapshot, in a separate folder

ssl.customHint: Use your own certificate (for example EV, or from another CA). It must cover the domain and match the key.
ssl.customRemoveHint: The site goes back to Let's Encrypt, and a certificate for all its current names is requested.
ssl.hstsHint: Makes browsers always use HTTPS. Only available with a valid certificate.
ssl.hstsWarning: For a year, browsers will refuse any non-HTTPS connection to this domain, even if the certificate stops working.
ssl.leHint: Free certificate, renewed automatically 30 days before it expires.
ssl.noAcmeEmail: No certificate requested: set the ACME e-mail in Settings, then issue the certificate.
ssl.wildcardHint: A wildcard covers {domain} and *.{domain} through Cloudflare DNS: it needs the token in Settings.

db.consoleHint: Read-only queries run as a user that can only read.
db.exportStarted: Export started: find it under Files › shared/exports
db.importCard: Path to a .sql file uploaded under Files.
db.importHint: The database will be replaced with {path}. A safety dump is taken first.
db.name: Name
db.writeHint: The query can change or delete production data.

dbs.databasesHint: Each database belongs to this site. Nothing is created by default for a static or plain PHP site; WordPress, WooCommerce and Laravel start with the primary one their configuration uses.
dbs.nameHint: Lowercase letters, digits and _, 3–48 characters, starting with a letter
dbs.nameRule: Use lowercase letters, digits and _ (3–48 characters), starting with a letter
dbs.dropHint: Every table in it is deleted. Its backups are kept: the retention policy removes them later.
dbs.noDatabasesHint: This site has none: nothing is created by default for a static or plain PHP site. Create one when the site needs it.
dbs.primaryHint: The database the site’s configuration (wp-config.php) uses
dbs.primaryKept: The primary database cannot be deleted: the site uses it
dbs.usersHint: A user signs in to MariaDB with its own password and reaches only the databases it is given: all privileges, or read only.
dbs.passwordHelp: Leave it empty to have a strong password generated (shown once). At least 12 characters if you choose one.
dbs.dropUserHint: Applications that sign in as this user stop reaching the database.
dbs.primaryUserHint: The user the site’s configuration (wp-config.php) signs in with
dbs.primaryUserKept: The primary user cannot be deleted: the site signs in with it
dbs.resetWordPress: wp-config.php is updated with the new password at the same time.
dbs.resetPrimary: The site signs in as this user: update its configuration (.env) with the new password.
dbs.passwordOnce: This password is shown only now. Copy it somewhere safe: the panel cannot show it again.

files.deleteDir: The folder and everything inside it will be deleted.
files.hint: Up to {size} per file here; use SFTP for larger transfers. Drop files or folders on the list to upload them.
files.binaryHint: This file is not text, so it cannot be edited here: download it instead.
files.tooLargeHint: Larger than {size}, too big for the editor: download it, or edit it over SFTP.

cron.wpHint: WordPress cron already runs from the system every 5 minutes; add your own here.
cron.footnote: A task runs as the site’s user, inside its folder. One that is off keeps its schedule for when it is turned on again.

php.hint: Per-site limits. Applying reloads only this site’s PHP pool: no request is lost.
php.title: PHP settings
php.versionGone: In use, no longer installed on the server.
php.versionDefault: Installed · the default for new sites.
php.workersHint: How many requests PHP serves at once. Left at 0, they are sized from the server’s memory and the site’s traffic.
php.workersPeak: At their memory limit, up to {mb} MB together.
php.budgetRefused: {workers} workers × {mb} MB is {total} MB, more than the memory budget ({budget} MB): lower one of them.

sftp.hint: An account confined to the site's folder: no shell, no access to other sites. Off until you turn it on.
sftp.keysHint: Recommended for developers. Every key has a type: “SFTP only” transfers files; “shell” also opens a terminal in the site while the shell below is on. Keys work only while SFTP access is on.
sftp.title: SFTP access
sftp.offHint: Choose how to sign in to turn it on. SSH keys only work while access is on.
sftp.shellKeyPending: While the shell is off, a “shell” key works as “SFTP only”: the terminal opens once the shell below is turned on.
sftp.shellHint: A terminal inside the site, for wp-cli, composer and git. It runs as the site’s user in the site’s folder, so new files get the right owner, in the same sandbox and with the same CPU and memory limits as the site’s PHP.
sftp.shellAdminOnly: Only an administrator can change this.
sftp.shellWarning: A shell runs any command as this site’s user: whoever holds a “shell” key can read and change the site’s files and its database credentials. Other sites and the server’s system stay out of reach, and there is no sudo.
sftp.shellNeedsAccess: The shell signs in only while SFTP access is on.
sftp.shellPreviewLabel: Shell preview: wp plugin list inside the site
sftp.shellFactTools: wp, composer, git and php; node if the server has it
sftp.shellFactIsolation: other sites and the server’s configuration are not there at all; no sudo, a private /tmp, other users’ processes invisible
sftp.shellFactEnd: everything a session starts ends with it, when the shell is turned off, and with the site
sftp.shellFactRelease: a checkout in ~/src can become a release (cgctl deploy), with rollback
sftp.confirmShellOn: Turn on the SSH shell for {site}?
sftp.confirmShellOff: Turn off the SSH shell? Open sessions end now.
sftp.confirmShellKeys: These keys will open a shell: {keys}.
sftp.confirmShellNoKeys: No key has the type “shell” yet: add one after turning the shell on.
sftp.shellKeyAdminOnly: Only an administrator can add a “shell” key.
sftp.modeKeysHint: Recommended. There is no password to guess: the server does not even ask for one.
sftp.modePasswordHint: The password is guessable from anywhere: against repeated attempts only the SSH server’s own limits apply for now.
sftp.firstKeyHint: The site has no SSH key yet: paste the one that will sign in.

migration.confirmBoth: The site's current files and database will be replaced. A restore point is created first.
migration.confirmFiles: The site's current files will be replaced. A restore point is created first.
migration.expansionLimitHint: Administrators only. How many times its compressed size the archive may expand to: 200 when empty, at most 1000.
migration.hint: Upload large files over SFTP first. CloudGround refuses unsafe links and paths in the archive, creates a fresh release and a database restore point, then switches everything at once.
migration.oldDomainHint: optional; safely rewrites serialized WordPress URLs
migration.title: Import an existing site

logs.hint: System and service logs. Each site's own logs are on its Logs tab.

services.restartHint: Requests in flight may fail for a few seconds.
services.hint: The system services that run the sites. A restart interrupts requests in flight for a few seconds.

firewall.enableHint: The firewall is off, so every port on this server is open. Turning it on first allows these rules, so SSH, the sites and the panel stay reachable, then blocks every other incoming connection.
firewall.inactiveRules: The firewall is inactive: these rules are stored, and apply only once it is enabled.
firewall.ruleHint: SSH, ports 80 and 443 and the panel's 8443 always stay open to everyone. For tighter security, restrict SSH and the panel to your IPs.

service.ssh: SSH, the port sshd listens on

users.name: Name
users.disableHint: Cannot sign in, and their sessions are closed.
users.resetDone: Password reset: their sessions were closed

security.disableHint: The account will be protected by its password alone.
security.disableWithPassword: To turn it off, enter your password
security.passwordHint: The panel has root on this server: use a long, unique password.
security.scan: Scan the code with Google Authenticator, 1Password or Authy, then enter the 6-digit code.
security.totpHint: A second factor from an authenticator app. Strongly recommended.
security.profileHint: The name you appear under in the panel and the audit log.
security.tokensHint: For cgctl and scripts. A token acts as the administrator who made it; it is managed from a signed-in session only.
security.tokenOnce: Copy the token now: it is not shown again.
security.tokenRevokeHint: Scripts using it are refused from their next request.
security.enrolRequired: Set up two-factor authentication to continue
security.enrolRequiredHint: This panel requires 2FA for administrators. Until you enrol, only this page is available; your profile, password and API tokens come back once 2FA is on.

settings.acmeHint: Used to register and for expiry notices.
settings.attached: The panel answers on {domain}, with a certificate that renews automatically.
settings.backupsHint: Backups are encrypted before they leave the server and run on each site's schedule.
settings.cloudflareHint: Zone:DNS:Edit permission; only needed for wildcard certificates.
settings.movePanel: Move the panel to this domain
settings.needAcme: Set the Let's Encrypt email below first.
settings.notificationsHint: Failed backups and restore tests, expiring certificates, stopped services, changed configuration.
settings.panelCertStarted: Certificate requested: once it is issued, the panel answers on the new domain, without a restart.
settings.panelDomainHint: The panel always answers on https://IP:8443. Point a domain at this server and secure it with a certificate that renews by itself: the panel will also answer on https://domain.
settings.probeTargetHint: Where Safe Push sends its measurement requests: always this server.
settings.repoPasswordHint: Losing this password means losing the backups.
settings.repositoryHint: S3, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, SFTP or a local folder.
settings.require2faHint: An administrator without 2FA sees only their own Security page until they enrol, so nobody is locked out.
settings.securePanel: Secure the panel with Let's Encrypt
settings.updateChannelHint: Stable installs only final versions. Beta also offers pre-release versions, to try changes before they ship.
settings.updateCheck: Check for updates when the panel is opened
settings.updateHint: Downloads the latest signed binaries and restarts the panel.
settings.updatesHint: Updates are signed: the panel installs only verified binaries.
settings.webhookHint: An https URL from Slack, Discord, Mattermost or similar (text field).

dbstudio.title: @:{'studio.name'}
dbstudio.intro: Browse and edit tables, run SQL, export and import, with the panel's sign-in, roles and audit.
dbstudio.rowsEstimate: Row counts are the server's estimate for InnoDB tables.
dbstudio.name: Name
dbstudio.alterHint: The ALTER statement is shown before it runs.
dbstudio.alterPreviewHint: On a large table it can take a while and lock writes.
dbstudio.defaultHint: Numbers as they are, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP for time columns; backslashes are not accepted.
dbstudio.prefixLengthHint: Text and blob columns need a prefix length to be indexed.
dbstudio.noPrimaryKey: This table has no primary key, so its rows cannot be edited here: use the SQL editor.
dbstudio.editHint: Double-click a cell to edit its row. Every change shows its SQL first and runs in a transaction.
dbstudio.binaryLocked: Binary column: edit it with the SQL editor.
dbstudio.cutLocked: Value too long to edit here: use the SQL editor.
dbstudio.changePreviewHint: It runs in a transaction and is rolled back if it does not touch exactly one row.
dbstudio.readOnlyAccount: Read-only account: statements run as a user that can only read.
dbstudio.sqlLimits: One statement at a time; at most 5000 rows or 8 MiB are shown and a statement is stopped after 60 seconds. Ctrl/Cmd+Enter runs.
dbstudio.historyEmpty: Statements you run appear here (kept in this browser only).
dbstudio.truncated: The result was cut at the limit.
dbstudio.exportHint: Written to shared/exports as a background task, then downloaded from the list below.
dbstudio.allTablesHint: Leave empty for the whole database.
dbstudio.importsHint: Uploaded .sql and .csv files, kept in shared/imports.
dbstudio.uploadHint: A .sql or .csv file, sent in 8 MiB pieces: large dumps work too.
dbstudio.badFileType: Only .sql and .csv files can be imported.
dbstudio.chooseTable: Choose the table to import the CSV into
dbstudio.importSqlHint: {name} will be run against the database. A rollback point is saved first, and restored if the import fails.
dbstudio.importCsvHint: The first row of {name} names the columns. All rows are inserted in one transaction.
dbstudio.transferReadOnly: Export and import need an administrator or operator account.
dbstudio.dataReadOnly: Table rows and the SQL editor need an administrator or operator account: a read-only account sees the tables and their structure.
dbstudio.notWordPress: These tools are for WordPress sites.
dbstudio.autoloadHint: Options WordPress loads on every request.
dbstudio.autoloadWarn: Over 800 KB of autoloaded options slows every uncached request: look at the largest ones below.
dbstudio.searchReplaceHint: Through wp-cli, so serialized data stays valid. GUIDs are left alone. A dry run counts the replacements first.
dbstudio.replaceConfirm: {n} replacements of “{from}” with “{to}” will be made.
dbstudio.transientsHint: Cached values whose time is up and that WordPress has not removed yet.

vhost.adminOnly: Only an administrator can see and change a site's routing.
vhost.hint: The location blocks below decide what serves each URL of the site: a front controller, an SPA's client-side routes, real 404 pages, a proxied /api, redirects. They start from the site type's default routing and you can change them freely.
vhost.loadFailed: Could not read the site's routing
vhost.managed: TLS and certificates, the page cache and its bypass rules, the security headers, the PHP-FPM link and the limits stay managed by the panel. They are shown read-only above and below the editor and cannot be overridden here.
vhost.notEditable: This site has no routing block to edit.
vhost.panelPart: Managed by the panel · {n} lines, read-only
vhost.refused: Not saved. The site keeps its previous routing
vhost.restoreHint: Your location blocks are replaced by the site type's default routing.
vhost.testedHint: nginx tests every change before it goes live. A change it rejects is not applied.
vhost.title: Routing and vhost

address.title: Domains and folder
address.hint: The other names the site answers to, and the folder of the release it serves. Applying re-renders the site.
address.aliasesHint: Up to 50 host names, each pointing at this server. A Let’s Encrypt certificate is issued again to cover them.
address.publicRootHint: A folder inside the release, such as public; empty serves the release itself. A folder that passes through a link is refused.
address.upstreamHint: The http(s) address the site forwards requests to.
address.customCertWarning: This site serves a custom certificate, which may not cover the new aliases: install one that does.

newSite.title: New
newSite.summaryHint: Everything you need to use the site. The database password is shown only here.
newSite.upstreamHelp: nginx proxies it with HTTP/3 and a certificate; the cache stays off until you turn it on.
newSite.withDatabaseHint: A MariaDB database and a user with all privileges on it.
newSite.dbAlways: A {type} site always has a database: its configuration uses it.
newSite.dbPasswordHelp: Generated for you; you can type your own. It is shown once more in the summary, then never again.
newSite.nameReserved: This name is reserved by the server
newSite.dbPasswordSpaces: It cannot start or end with a space
newSite.willBackups: nightly backups with a restore test
newSite.sftpOff: off: turn it on from the SFTP tab (user {user})
newSite.onceHint: The database password is not shown again. Download or copy the summary; a new password can be set later from the Database tab.
newSite.closeHint: You have neither downloaded nor copied the summary: the database password will not be shown again.
newSite.txtSecret: This file contains passwords. Keep it somewhere safe and delete it once you have stored them elsewhere.
newSite.nameTaken: {name} is already used on this server

studio.signInHint: Use a database user's own name and password. You see and change exactly what MariaDB grants that user.
studio.fromPanel: Signed in to the panel? Open @:{'studio.name'} from a site’s Database tab instead.
studio.openingHint: Signing in with your panel session…
studio.handoffMissing: This page needs a link from the panel. Open @:{'studio.name'} again from the site’s Database tab.
studio.noDatabasesHint: This session cannot open any database.
studio.routineHint: Stored routines are listed; @:{'studio.name'} does not run or change them.
studio.sqlAsUser: Runs as {user}: MariaDB decides what it may do.
studio.searchHint: Finds the rows that contain the text in any text column, table by table.
studio.searchTableHint: Shows the rows of this table that contain the text in any text column.
studio.searchTruncated: The search stopped at its limit: not every table was searched.
studio.importAsUser: {name} runs as {user}, statement by statement. There is no rollback point: if a statement fails, what ran before it stays.
studio.importNoRollback: As a database user, an SQL import has no rollback point: export the database first if you may need it back.
studio.dropHint: The table and every row in it are deleted. This cannot be undone.
studio.truncateHint: Every row is deleted; the structure stays. This cannot be undone.
studio.insertHint: Every value is shown as SQL before it is inserted.
studio.panelHint: @:{'studio.name'} opens in a new tab, signed in for this site. A database user can also sign in to it at /quarry with its own password.
studio.name: Quarry
studio.explainHint: Show how MariaDB would run the statement (EXPLAIN), without running it
studio.simulateHint: Run an UPDATE, DELETE, INSERT or REPLACE in a transaction that is always rolled back, to see how many rows it would change
studio.simulateLimits: Simulate runs a write in a transaction that is always rolled back; what cannot be rolled back (DDL, MyISAM tables, triggers) is refused.
studio.simulateErrorRolledBack: The server refused the statement; the transaction was rolled back
studio.simulateRolledBack: The statement ran in a transaction that was rolled back: nothing was changed.
studio.simulatePreview: Matching rows as they are now ({n} shown, at most 25)
